title: dataframe_graph_input_fingerprint hand-rolls json.dumps instead of the mandated single canonical_json encoder
description: The digest here is produced with json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')).encode() rather than haute._cache.canonical_json. canonical_json's docstring is explicit that it is THE only canonical-JSON encoder for digest material and that adding a second divergent encoder is how silent cache collisions / phantom invalidations arise ('do not add a second one; import this'). The sibling module _dataframe_execution_cache.py follows this (dataframe_execution_policy_fingerprint and dataframe_execution_cache_key both use canonical_json), and ALGO_VERSION v5 exists specifically to record that the two divergent encoders were unified. For the payload this function actually builds (str keys, dict/list/scalar values only) json.dumps and canonical_json emit identical bytes, so this is behaviour-preserving today; but it re-introduces a forbidden second encoder and leaves a latent divergence for any future extra_fingerprints value that is a set/tuple or a non-finite float, where the two encoders disagree (canonical_json normalises sets and emits deterministic Infinity/NaN/array ordering). Replace with: content_hash_bytes(canonical_json(payload).encode()) and drop the local json import use here.
evidence: execution.py:509 returns content_hash_bytes(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')).encode()). _cache.py:71-100 canonical_json docstring mandates single encoder; _dataframe_execution_cache.py:212 and :288 use canonical_json for the very keys this fingerprint feeds into. _cache.py:46 ALGO_VERSION v5 comment: the two divergent encoders were replaced by canonical_json.
est_reduction: 1 line changed; removes one of two JSON-digest encoders the codebase forbids
behavior_preservation: Byte-identical digest for all current inputs (str-keyed dict/list/scalar payloads); only diverges for set/tuple/non-finite values, which this function does not currently receive.
